result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For a small team, I'd recommend **1Password** as the best overall password manager.

It's particularly good for businesses with around 3–30 people because it combines secure password sharing, straightforward administration, easy onboarding and offboarding, and strong security features without requiring a dedicated IT administrator.

However, there are a few good alternatives depending on your budget and technical requirements.

## My top 3

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password** (Best overall)

- Excellent shared vaults and permissions.
- Easy for non-technical staff.
- Good admin controls and security alerts.
- Teams Starter Pack: US\$24.95/month for 10 users, billed annually.
- [Pricing and plans](https://1password.com/pricing/business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

![‎Bitwarden App - App Store](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/x38pyi5v1Vy6Zs97qz8ZgS0U3TY6bP46EZUol0vjWY-QJEsjpBL1sBYpo0AxExRZj59SXzc9D5J1hCMKpLCQRKtRmi0IYkc0CeiDQsrny4xPWuRz2OGsqZ9tyuMm4GtN5vMAwBBf6hXgHDHMP9_wXSBVttW9bXO5pQrWG4hhS-RxRNQIRTsbPrqb3y45Jv-M?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden** (Best value)

- Open-source software.
- Strong team sharing and administration.
- Good choice for technically minded teams.
- Teams plan: around US\$4/user/month, billed annually.
- [Pricing and plans](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![‎Keeper Password Manager‑App – App Store](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/9fFOhO1vgUi3iQzGjCqH7JqTpnNusuz8g5CxIDGas4fIJyoDN5ACmEIAl0f7t_fD5APaWvKtb4us219T6A7CK54ed4xLKjytjzznq5HYY0f5wucW6T63yx_oUWBr0bvw6eDVbEfEp9P48IsFSm0sGGHZofY3rtEWKFKDED5LPJhb002Zp-VR5rXWAl4lz2jg?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Good administrative controls.
- Shared folders and delegated access.
- Worth considering if compliance and access management are important.
- [Business plans](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

Prices are indicative USD prices, before tax; check current Australian pricing at checkout. [1password.com](https://1password.com/pricing/business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[geekchamp.com](https://geekchamp.com/best-password-managers-for-small-business-teams-with-shared-access-controls/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd insist on for a business

Whichever one you choose, make sure it supports\:

- **Shared vaults\:** Share credentials without sending passwords through Slack or email.
- **Individual accounts\:** Never have everyone share one master login.
- **Access controls\:** Give people access only to the credentials they need.
- **Easy offboarding\:** Revoke access immediately when someone leaves.
- **MFA\:** Require multifactor authentication for every employee.
- **Audit logs\:** Know who accessed or changed shared credentials.

## My recommendation

I'd shortlist 1Password and Bitwarden\:

| Your priority | Choose |
|--------|--------|
| Easiest for everyone to use | 1Password |
| Best value for money | Bitwarden |
| More advanced administration | Keeper |


For most small businesses, I'd pay a little extra for 1Password if it means employees actually adopt it and use it consistently.
